docs.title: Welcome to the Agentic Testing for Business People Workshop
docs.text:
Thank you for joining the UiPath Agentic Testing for Business People Workshop!

This Learner's Handbook is your hands-on guide for the day. It answers one business question: can UiBank ship its new loan form?

You follow a release the way your team does: from a requirement, to test cases, to test runs, to reports, to a go/no-go decision. No code. AI helps at every step, and you stay in charge of every decision.

Before the workshop

Complete the Prerequisites before the session starts. You install UiPath Assistant with Delegate on your Windows laptop or Mac, and connect Delegate to Test Manager once (about 5 minutes). Everything else runs in your browser.

Your trainer will share the organization and tenant you'll use during the workshop.

Labels may differ on your tenant

This workshop runs on a tenant with the latest features. Your own tenant may show slightly different labels, or may not have every feature yet. Features marked (Preview) may still change.

docs.title: Your three helpers
docs.text:
You'll work with three kinds of helper. Each one has its own job.

✅ Autopilot in Test Manager – AI built into Test Manager. Its buttons check a requirement, generate test cases and write reports. Its chat answers questions about your project, builds charts and organizes your work, such as creating a test set.

✅ Delegate on your desktop – an AI agent on your laptop that works in your apps the way you would. Today it runs a test case on the UiBank website, and reproduces a defect with screenshots.

✅ Robots – they run tests for you, without anyone at the keyboard. Your trainer provides them: one robot follows your written test steps on its own, and cloud robots run the automated regression tests.

See Introduction for which helper to use when.

docs.title: What you'll do
docs.text:
The day follows a release from start to finish, in four phases:

Phase 1 · Prepare Requirement + tests 1Import and meet Autopilot chat 2Evaluate the requirement 3Generate test cases A clear requirement and test cases you trust, with Autopilot Phase 2 · Run You, Delegate, a robot 4Run the test three ways 5Compare the runs One test, three testers, and the evidence each one leaves Phase 3 · Automate & organize Studio Web + chat 6Automate with Studio Web 7Build and run the regression set A regression set built in chat and run on cloud robots Phase 4 · Decide Reports + decision 8Read the results 9Decide go or no-go Charts, reports and a documented go/no-go decision

Select a step to jump to it.

The day runs from 09:00 to 17:00, with two breaks and lunch. The robot works through everyone's test runs over lunch, so you start it just before.

docs.title: Who is it for
docs.text:
The workshop is for mixed business teams: business analysts (BA), user acceptance testing (UAT) testers, and test or quality assurance (QA) managers. Each step shows who leads it: BA UAT QA or All. Everyone does every step.

Hover over or select a card to see what you take home.

Business analyst (BA) What you take home
  • Measurable acceptance criteria
  • Test cases generated from a requirement
  • Coverage gaps found in chat
UAT tester What you take home
  • A manual run with evidence
  • The same test run by Delegate and a robot
  • Steps an agent can follow
Test / QA manager (QA) What you take home
  • A regression set run without code
  • Charts and reports you can check
  • A go/no-go decision with evidence

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
By the end of the workshop, every learner can:

✅ Explain in plain words what Autopilot in Test Manager (buttons and chat), Delegate and a test robot each do, and pick the right one for a job

✅ Explain MCP (Model Context Protocol) as "the list of approved actions Autopilot chat can take in Test Manager", and approve one of those actions

✅ Know the cost basics: Autopilot chat turns and Delegate tasks use your AI allowance, Autopilot buttons don't, and robot runs use the tenant's Platform Units

Objectives by role

Business analyst (BA)

✅ Evaluate a requirement with Autopilot, and turn vague rules into measurable acceptance criteria

✅ Generate test cases from a requirement and its documents, then judge which to keep. Optional: import existing Excel UAT scripts

✅ Use Autopilot chat to find coverage gaps, such as test cases with no requirement

✅ Optional: turn a business document into a requirement and a test case with Delegate

UAT tester

✅ Run a manual test and record evidence: pass or fail, a comment, a screenshot

✅ Hand the same test case to Delegate and to a robot, and compare the evidence each one leaves

✅ Write test steps that both a person and an agent can follow

✅ Tell a UiBank defect from a test defect, and reproduce it with evidence

Test / QA manager

✅ Build a regression set with Autopilot chat, and run it on cloud robots without code

✅ Read Dashboard numbers correctly: Total Coverage means "a test exists", not "ready to release"

✅ Build charts in chat, and check the AI's counts against Execution

✅ Produce an Execution Insights report and an execution PDF

✅ Make and document a go/no-go decision based on the requirement, not on the success rate. Optional: formal sign-off

docs.text:
Section What's inside Prerequisites Your laptop and browser, your account, and installing and connecting Delegate Introduction A short tour of Test Cloud and Test Manager, and which helper to use when Hands-On Workshop The nine hands-on steps, from importing your project to the go/no-go decision Troubleshooting & Next Steps More prompts to try, fixes for common problems, and how to take this to your team Trainer Setup The trainer's checklist before the workshop

Here's something worth holding onto as you work through this workshop

AI agents don't replace testers – they give testers a new way to work. Instead of clicking through dashboards to find out what failed and why, you ask a question in plain English and get an answer grounded in your real test data.

Robots bring determinism and control, agents bring adaptability and reasoning. This workshop is about putting the two together.

Next → Prerequisites

docs.title: Trainer Setup
docs.text:
Complete this page a few days before the workshop, then run the day-before checklist. It sets up one shared folder, two kinds of cloud robot, a Trainer Demo project with a published Studio Web package, and the backups you need if something fails in class.

Where these steps come from

Most steps below were done and checked on a Test Cloud tenant in November 2026, with one trainer account and one learner-like account. Steps marked not tested or re-checked in the rehearsal were not – check them with a learner-only account before the class. Use your Test Cloud host wherever the guide says <host>. Labels may differ slightly on your tenant, and (Preview) features may change.

What you build

Object Name used in the guide Used in Shared Orchestrator folder ATB - Agentic Testing Workshop (plain hyphen) every step (Default Folder, step 1) Robot account one unattended robot account, for example ATB Workshop Robot steps 4, 5, 7 Cloud Robot – VM pool runtime type Cloud - VM Testing steps 4 and 5 (Run autonomously, Autonomous Exploration) Cloud Robot – Serverless machine runtime type Cloud - Serverless Testing step 7 (regression set) Trainer Demo project your own name and prefix, for example ATB Trainer Demo demos and backups Studio Web Tests project and package UiBank.BusinessTests steps 6 and 7

docs.title: Organization and tenant
docs.text:
✅ A Test Cloud organization on Unified Pricing. Autopilot chat, its charts, Run autonomously, Autonomous Exploration, governance and running a test case without a test set need Test Manager on Test Cloud. They aren't available on Flex licensing.

✅ Learners can join the organization. Either the organization allows external users (learners sign in with their own accounts), or you invite learners with company accounts.

✅ Services: the tenant has Test Manager, Orchestrator and Studio Web enabled.

✅ Licence plan: open Admin → Licenses and check which plan the organization is on. It decides how much AI each learner gets (see Licences and usage).

✅ AI Trust Layer policy: in Automation Ops → Governance, an AI Trust Layer policy is active and deployed to the tenant, with Feature Toggles → Enabling Test Manager features set to Yes. User License Management is enabled for the organization. In Admin → AI Trust Layer → Model hub, check that no strict data-residency rule blocks the models Test Manager uses. See About Autopilot chat and Enabling/disabling Autopilot.

✅ Automation Ops Autopilot policy: if your organization uses one, check that it doesn't block the Test Manager tools or MCP servers (it controls tools, MCP servers, security mode and models). Learners use the built-in Test Manager MCP server in step 7. See Architecture and data flow.

✅ Automation Ops Assistant policy: check that Delegate isn't switched off for learners, and that the approval mode isn't locked to a setting that blocks the exercises. See Settings for Assistant policies.

Check it

With a learner-like account: open any Test Manager project and check that the Autopilot icon is in the top bar (it isn't on the project list). Open a requirement → + Evaluate quality is available.

docs.title: Users and licences
docs.text:
✅ Your trainer account: your own account needs an App Test Developer licence, the Project Creator tenant role in Test Manager, Folder Administrator on the workshop folder, and tenant-level rights to publish packages: the tenant role Allow to be Automation Publisher plus a folder role that can publish, such as Automation Publisher (both labels confirmed on the rehearsal tenant). On your laptop, install UiPath Assistant signed in to the same tenant, and the UiPath Studio Web browser extension, for Indicate target and the Autopilot Recorder.

✅ Create a group for the learners, invite each learner to the organization, and add them to the group. Give rights and licences to the group, so late joiners get everything at once.

✅ Licence: allocate App Test Developer to the group (Admin → Licenses). App Tester is the minimum: it has Autopilot chat and Delegate, but can't build in Studio Web. Never use Express User. Autopilot chat in Test Manager isn't included with a Pro licence. See User licenses.

✅ Test Manager: give the group the Project Creator tenant role, so each learner can import and own a project in step 1.

Tenant role, not a project role

Project Creator is a tenant role. No Test Manager project role can create projects. The learner who imports the project becomes its owner and can set the Default Folder and use governance without extra grants. See Tenant roles and project roles.

✅ Orchestrator access rule for the group: in Orchestrator, at the Tenant level, open Manage access (Access → Access rules in the new layout) → Assign access → Groups, pick the group, and:

✅ under Roles, add Allow to be Automation User (learners don't publish, so they don't need Automation Developer or Publisher)

✅ under Settings, set Personal automation setup to Enable personal automation (with or without Personal workspace). Delegate needs Personal Automation.

The screenshot comes from a developer workshop and shows broader roles. For this workshop, Allow to be Automation User is enough – it carries Packages – View, which Select Automation needs to list the Tenant Package Feed. See Proven minimum rights.

Check it

In Admin → Licenses → Users, each learner has App Test Developer (or App Tester), directly or through the group. No Autopilot icon for a learner inside a project? This row is the first thing to check.

docs.title: Licences and usage
docs.text:
Item What to check AI and Agentic usage pool Each chat turn and each Delegate task uses the learner's monthly pool. Autopilot buttons (Evaluate quality, Generate tests, Generate Report) don't. On an Enterprise plan, App Tester gets 7x the Basic pool and App Test Developer 20x. On Basic and trial plans, every licence except Express User gets the same Basic pool. When the pool is spent, Autopilot and Delegate pause: there is no fallback to paid units. Budget per learner: about 11 chat turns, plus 4–5 Delegate tasks. On a Basic or trial plan, UiPath's own estimate puts the Basic pool at about 4 chat tasks and 2 standard Delegate tasks a month, below the 4–5 the workshop uses. Plan a top-up for every learner, or run the Delegate parts as trainer demos. See Methodology for usage estimates and Usage pool consumption Top-ups Granting a top-up needs the License Administrator role and Platform Units in the organization's distribution. One pack = 50 Platform Units, and granted packs can't be returned. Option for a class: turn on Automatic License Top-Up Grant (Preview) in the AI Trust Layer policy. Bring your own model (BYOM) for Delegate, if your organization allows it, avoids the pool. See Granting AI and agentic usage top-ups App Test Platform Units Run autonomously and Autonomous Exploration need an active App Test Platform Units bundle on the tenant. The docs publish no rate per run: note the balance before and after the pre-warm runs. See Autonomous test execution Platform Units for robots The Cloud Robot – VM pool deducts Platform Units per month from the tenant balance; serverless robots are billed per minute. See Machine sizes and costs Trainer FAQ: \"Do the buttons really cost nothing?\"

The learner pages cite only the testing usage-pool page, which says a capability called through its own button never uses the pool. A different page, Autopilot for Everyone licensing, describes the older Autopilot for Everyone meter (0.2 Platform Units per action after a monthly limit). If a sharp learner or admin finds it, that is the explanation. See Autopilot usage pool for testing.

docs.title: The shared folder
docs.text:
All learners work in one Orchestrator folder. They do no Orchestrator work themselves: they only pick this folder as their project's Default Folder in step 1.

Orchestrator asks you to choose a layout?

This page uses the classic tab names (Folders, Machines, Manage access), with the new-layout name in brackets. See the New layout navigation map.

  1. In Orchestrator, at the Tenant level, open Folders (Access → Folder management).

  2. Click the new folder icon next to Manage Folders.

  3. Enter the Name ATB - Agentic Testing Workshop with a plain hyphen (learners type it in a search box), keep Process packages source as Tenant package feed, and click Create.

    Create it where learners get no inherited roles

    Create the folder at the root, or under a parent folder where the learner group has no role. A folder under a parent where a learner group is Folder Administrator inherits that role, gives learners admin rights, and hides any rights problem until a real class.

  4. Create a custom folder role for learners: Orchestrator → Tenant → Roles (Access → Roles) → Add role → type Folder, name it for example ATB Workshop Learner, and grant only the View permission for subfolders (API name SubFolders.View; the role editor lists it under Subfolders or Folders, depending on the layout).

  5. Open the folder → Manage access → Assign account/group/external app:

    • the learner group (or each learner): folder roles Automation User and your learner role from item 4
    • your trainer or admin group: Folder Administrator

    In the rehearsal, Test Manager's Default Folder picker listed the folder only after a direct folder assignment for the learner. A group assignment wasn't tested: check it with a learner account.

  6. Select Check own permissions and tick View Inherited Users to see the effective rights.

docs.title: Proven minimum rights
docs.text:
Rehearsed on 2026-11-22 with a learner account that had no admin role anywhere:

Where What the learner needs Why Licence App Test Developer (or App Tester), direct or through the group Autopilot, Autopilot chat, Delegate Tenant – Orchestrator Allow to be Automation User (through the learner group) Packages – View for Select Automation (Tenant Package Feed) Tenant – Test Manager Project Creator (through the learner group) Import and own a project (step 1) Workshop folder Automation User + the learner role with subfolder View (items 4–5 above) Default Folder, Run autonomously, serverless runs

With exactly these rights, all of these worked: Default Folder (save and reload), Run autonomously (package upload, process create, job – one run passed in 7 min 50 s), Select Automation and Save from the Tenant Package Feed, the serverless regression set (2/1/0), the chat write tools Bulk_add_labels, Create_test_set and Assign_test_cases_to_test_set, Execution Insights, the PDF download, a deactivated schedule, and governance with the learner as their own approver.

Without the subfolder View permission

With Automation User alone, the Default Folder picker lists the workshop folder and Save works, but Project Settings then shows the toast Folder does not exist. and the Default Folder field is blank after a reload. Add the learner role from item 4 and reload – no change in the learner's project is needed.

Button-made suggestions can't be applied by learners

Suggestions created by the + Evaluate quality button returned a rights error when the learner clicked Add to Requirement or changed a status ("You do not have the necessary rights to access this application.", with a Click here to logout button – PATCH …/llmactivity = 403), also with the old admin group restored for a test. Suggestions created through Autopilot chat (the same evaluation, via the chat prompt and its Review button) could be applied and their status changed, in the new and in the old learner project. Step 2 sends learners to the chat route when the error appears.

To link an automation for a learner (step 6 fallback), do it at their desk, in their browser and their project. Or ask them to add you in their project's Project Settings → Manage Access → Assign users/groups with the Test Manager Administrator project role (project role labels seen: Project Owner, Test Manager, Viewer, Test Manager Administrator).

Fallback: one folder per learner

If one shared folder doesn't suit your tenant, create one folder per learner, and add the robot account and both machines to each folder. It costs about 4 minutes of setup per learner.

docs.title: Robot account
docs.text:
Learners' run panels pick Any User/Robot account. The folder needs one account that can run unattended jobs, or runs stay Pending.

  1. Create a robot account, for example ATB Workshop Robot (Admin → Accounts & groups → Robot accounts; labels may differ).
  2. In the workshop folder → Manage access → Assign account/group/external app, add the robot account with the folder role Automation User. If the panel asks for a tenant role, add Allow to be Automation User.
  3. Check that its Robot Type shows Unattended.

docs.title: Robots
docs.text:
Learners use two kinds of cloud robot. You don't install anything on learner laptops.

Robot Runtime type Runs Who starts it Cloud Robot – VM pool, Windows 11 Cloud - VM Testing Run autonomously (step 4), Autonomous Exploration (step 5 demo) – both (Preview) each learner (Run autonomously); you (Exploration) Cloud Robot – Serverless Cloud - Serverless Testing the automated regression set (step 7) each learner

docs.title: Cloud Robot – VM pool for Run autonomously and Exploration
docs.text:
Run autonomously and Autonomous Exploration run in the machine's default browser on a Cloud - VM Testing, Cloud - VM or self-hosted testing runtime. Serverless runtimes aren't supported for them. Autonomous Exploration needs a Windows robot; this workshop uses a Windows 11 pool for both.

  1. In Orchestrator, at the Tenant level, open Machines (Infrastructure → Machines) → Add machine → Cloud Robot - VM.

  2. Fill in the pool. The settings that were rehearsed:

    Setting Value Machine management Automatic (VMs are created and deleted for you; changes made on a VM don't persist) Pool environment Test – this gives the Cloud - VM Testing runtime type VM size Standard (4 CPUs, 32 GB) Machine image Windows Desktop → Standard → UiPath + Supported Browsers on Windows 11 Enterprise Machine availability profile Balanced normally; Always (or Fast) for the workshop day – see the capacity box Max number of VMs 1 to start; see the capacity box Automation Cloud Runtime(s) per machine 1; see the capacity box Runtime license Platform units (PLTUs) – the page shows the monthly total Pool configurations Allow UiPath to manage Robot updates on (required for a standard image)

  3. Open the workshop folder → Machines → Manage Machines in Folder, select the pool, and click Update.

No remote desktop session, browser extension setting or Allow in Incognito change was needed on the standard image: Run autonomously and Exploration both worked as delivered. Autopilot drove Edge on the VM. The robot log warns that the VM screen resolution 1024x768 is below the recommended 1920x1080 and "ScreenPlay executions may be less accurate": if runs misread the page, raise the resolution as the warning's docs link describes. See Running unattended automations using cloud robots – VM.

Capacity: plan the queue before lunch

Measured with 1 VM and 1 runtime on Balanced:

  • The first job of the day waited 9 minutes while a VM started. Balanced shuts an idle VM down again.
  • Each Run autonomously took about 6 minutes (5 min 43 s to 8 min 14 s), one after another per runtime. One runtime handles about 9–10 runs an hour.

Learners start Run autonomously at the start of step 4, so the queue drains over lunch. Aim for one VM per 4–5 learners (15 learners → 3 VMs). Both settings show their cost on the pool's edit page:

  • Max number of VMs: the lever to use. Each VM runs one browser job at a time and adds the VM size's monthly cost (600 Platform Units for Standard). For 15 learners, set 3 VMs.
  • Automation Cloud Runtime(s) per machine: leave at 1. The docs describe parallel jobs on extra runtimes for background processes only, and Run autonomously drives a browser. Each extra runtime still costs 400 Platform Units per VM per month.

For the workshop day, set Always (or start the pre-warm runs 15 minutes before class), check the Platform Units balance first, and revert the availability profile and Max number of VMs after the class.

What learners see

The Run autonomously panel preselects Cloud - VM Testing on a folder with this pool. Cloud - Serverless Testing and Cloud - Serverless are selectable in the list, but not supported. The learner pages say "your trainer tells you which runtime": tell them Cloud - VM Testing.

docs.title: Cloud Robot – Serverless for the regression set
docs.text:
1. At the Tenant level, open Machines → Add machine → Cloud Robot - Serverless. Enter a name, for example ATB Serverless, check that Cloud - Serverless Testing is offered as a runtime type, and select Provision.
  2. Open the workshop folder → Machines → Manage Machines in Folder, select the serverless machine, and click Update.
  3. Check the serverless capacity. The rehearsed folder showed one Cloud - Serverless Testing runtime. In the learner-like pass, start the regression set from two projects at once and check that both run in parallel. If they queue, raise the serverless runtimes for the folder, or allow a few extra minutes in step 7.

Serverless jobs are limited to 15 minutes; the 3-test regression set takes under a minute. Studio Web Tests projects are cross-platform, so they run on serverless robots. See Executing unattended automations with serverless robots.

Configure Automation may default to the VM pool

With both machines in the folder, a test set's Configure Automation panel preselected Cloud - VM Testing in one rehearsal and showed an empty Runtime type in another. Step 7 tells learners in bold to pick Cloud - Serverless Testing either way. A learner who misses it sends the regression run to the VM queue: cancel and run again.

docs.title: Robot-side errors
docs.text:
These happen on the robot, not in the learner's test. They used to be learner troubleshooting rows.

What learners see Cause and fix Tests fail with "Cannot communicate with the browser" The UiPath browser extension on the robot isn't reachable. On an automatically managed VM pool, use the standard image UiPath + Supported Browsers on Windows 11 Enterprise, which has the extension; on a custom image, install and enable the extension in the image. Then run again Tests fail with "Failed to start browser. New browser window did not appear." The robot opened a browser profile without the UiPath extension. Same fix as above: standard image, or a custom image with the extension on in the default profile. Then run again A run stays Pending The VM is starting (up to 9 minutes on Balanced), the queue is long, the folder has no unattended robot account, or a serverless runtime was picked for Run autonomously. Check Orchestrator → Jobs in the workshop folder A regression test shows Faulted in Orchestrator Jobs A test that fails its assertion shows as Faulted in Jobs. It isn't a robot error: check the test log in Test Manager

docs.title: Trainer Demo project and the Studio Web package
docs.text:
The Trainer Demo project is your own UiBank project. It holds the published automation that learners link to in step 6, and every backup.

  1. Import the workshop .tmh (step 1 of the learner guide) under a name and prefix of your own, for example ATB Trainer Demo. Set Project Settings → Automation → Default Folder to the workshop folder.
  2. Add a manual test case Submit Over-65 Request with the same data as the automation (amount 50000, term 3 years, income 90000, age 66). Expected result: rejected with "Not approved due to age." Link it to Submit Loan Request. Learners create the same test case, with the same data, in step 3.
  3. Give the learner group read-only access to this project: Project Settings → Manage Access → Assign users/groups, pick the group, and assign the Viewer project role (the label shown in Manage Access). Step 5 sends learners here to read your completed over-65 run. Without it, learners don't see the project at all – the rehearsal learner lost sight of it once its admin group was removed – so show the run on the projector instead. See Tenant roles and project roles.

docs.title: Build the package in Studio Web
docs.text:
Learners link to these four tests by name, so use these names exactly:

Studio Web test Test data Expected result in UiBank today Submit Standard Loan Request any test email, amount 50000, term 3, income 90000, age 34 passes – "Congrats! You've been approved…" Submit Underage Request same, age 17 passes – age 17 gives "Sorry, at this time you have not been approved for a loan." Submit Over-65 Request same, age 66 fails – age 66 gets "Congrats! You've been approved…", but the requirement says reject. This is the UiBank defect behind the NO-GO Submit High-Volume Request amount 150000, term 3, income 500000, age 34 fails – a spare: UiBank never approves loans over $100,000, although the requirement approves them when income is more than 3x the loan. The imported test case uses amount 120000 and income 90000. Change its steps 6, 8 and 11 to 150000, 500000 and "Verify 'Congrats! You've been approved…'", or chat calls its failure a test defect
  1. In Test Manager, open Submit Standard Loan Request → Automation tab → Automate in Studio Web.
  2. In the panel, type UiBank.BusinessTests in Project* and select Create project "UiBank.BusinessTests". In Test case*, create the test with the test case's name. Select Add automation. You see "Automation updated successfully!", then Open in Studio Web.
  3. Repeat for the other three test cases, choosing the same project.

  4. In Studio Web, build each test: Use Browser on https://uibank.uipath.com/loans/apply (Chrome) → Type Into email, amount, income and age → Select Item for the term → Click submit → Get Text of the heading on the result page → Verify Expression that it contains "Congrats" (approve) or "Sorry" (reject). Use the test data from the table.

    Use an amount of $100,000 or less in the Over-65 test. Otherwise UiBank rejects it for the amount and the defect is hidden.

    Indicate target and the Autopilot Recorder need the UiPath robot on your own machine ("Please wait while we start the UI Automation process on your local machine"): install UiPath Assistant on the trainer laptop and sign in to the same tenant first.

  5. Debug each test on the cloud (right-click the file → Debug). Standard passes ("Verification passed…"); Over-65 fails ("Verification failed. The expression 'resultHeading' with value 'Congrats!'…").

  6. Select Publish: choose Shared (confirm in the rehearsal), Version 1.0.0, and set Location to Orchestrator Tenant Processes Feed (the default differs by tenant – it was Orchestrator Autopilot Feed on the rehearsal tenant). Publish.
  7. Back in Test Manager, each linked test case now shows Package Source: Tenant Package Feed on its Automation tab.

The empty TestCase entry

Every Studio Web Tests project has a default TestCase entry point that can't be deleted. It shows up in learners' Select Automation list. Step 6 tells learners to ignore it.

One editor at a time

A shared Tests project allows one editor at a time, so learners don't open it. They link to the published package with Select Automation (step 6). Opening it read-only as a learner wasn't tested.

See Automating test cases in Studio Web, Publishing a project and Selecting automation.

docs.title: The live demo in step 6
docs.text: Demo on a test case with no automation yet, for example Submit Short-Term Request in the Trainer Demo project. Create a separate Tests project, for example UiBank.DemoLive, build or record one test and Debug it. Never publish UiBank.BusinessTests again during class – learners link version 1.0.0, and step 7 expects it.

docs.title: Run the regression set yourself
docs.text:
1. In the Trainer Demo project, create the test set Release 2.4 - Loan regression (plain hyphen) with Submit Standard Loan Request, Submit Underage Request and Submit Over-65 Request.
  2. Configure Automation → Runtime type = Cloud - Serverless Testing, Robot account = Any User/Robot account, Autoselect packages → UiBank.BusinessTests - 1.0.0 → Save.
  3. Execute → Automated. Expect 2 passed / 1 failed / 0 none in under a minute.

docs.title: Backups in the Trainer Demo project
docs.text:
Keep these ready in the Trainer Demo project, so any step can fall back to them:

✅ Completed Run autonomously runs – from the pre-warm (below), including one of Submit Over-65 Request that fails at the age decision. Step 5 sends learners to it when their own run hasn't finished. Learners open it through the Viewer role from the setup above; if that doesn't work on the day, show it on the projector.

✅ An Autonomous Exploration report – from the pre-warm.

✅ An Execution Insights report – Execution → Generate Report → From selection on your regression run → Reports tab → Download (DOCX).

✅ The reference execution PDF – the regression execution's download icon → Download Pdf. Keep an unsigned copy for learners. A PDF from a signed governed log contains the signer's name and email.

✅ A reference go/no-go report – the step 9 chat summary of your regression run, or a Delegate PDF report made from it. Unsigned, no names. It covers step 9 if a learner's chat or Delegate fails, or if UiBank fixes the defect.

✅ Offline copies – save the Insights DOCX, the unsigned execution PDF, the reference go/no-go report and screenshots of each step on your laptop. If the tenant is down, walk through them on the projector. Decide before the day whether a second tenant, set up the same way, is your backup.

✅ An Exploration charter prompt in Project Settings → Prompt Library, for example "Explore only the over-65 rule of the loan application form."

Optional: governance on the Trainer Demo project

Shows the formal sign-off box in step 9.

  1. Project Settings → Governance → Enable governance: set Default governance state (Governed / Not governed), Default approvers (users or groups) and Signing order, then Save.
  2. Logs created before you enabled governance aren't governed: open the log and switch the Governed toggle on.
  3. Set the approval status to In review. This locks the log: edits are disabled until all approvers sign.
  4. On the log's Governance tab, sign: Your role at time of signature*, optional comments, Sign. Self-approval was allowed in the rehearsal.

Signatures show the signer's name and email, also in the PDF: crop screenshots and don't share that PDF. See Testing process governance.

docs.title: Pre-warm the robots (the day before)
docs.text:
The first Run autonomously in a folder uploads a test package and creates the process UiPathTestCloudAutonomousTestExecution; the first Exploration creates UiPathTestCloudAutonomousExploration. Do these runs the day before, so the first class runs don't also start a cold VM.

  1. Run autonomously ×3 from the Trainer Demo project – Submit Over-65 Request (the step 5 backup), Submit Standard Loan Request and Submit Underage Request: test case ⋮ → Execute Autonomously → Url* https://uibank.uipath.com (the test cases start on the UiBank home page), keep the recommended Model, Next → Runtime type Cloud - VM Testing, Robot account Any User/Robot account → Run. Note the time per run and the App Test Platform Units used.

    The panel saves the Url into the test case's Manual Steps → URL field and pre-fills it next time. Typing into a pre-filled field appends to it: in the rehearsal that produced …/loans/applyhttps://…, and the next runs ended after step 1 with "Verification could not be completed (HttpRequestException)". Clear the field before you type, or set the URL once in Manual Steps. 2. Autonomous Exploration ×1: requirement Submit Loan Request → + Autonomous Exploration. A 10-minute time-box finished in 11 minutes and covered about one scenario. For the step 5 demo, use the narrow charter prompt ("only the over-65 rule"), or a 20–30 minute pre-run you show as the result. 3. Keep the completed runs and the report as backups. Check that Autopilot reached the over-65 age step and marked it Failed, with a screenshot of the approval page – that is the result learners compare in step 5 (the rehearsal's Trainer Demo run showed exactly that; see the warning below).

Check that behaviour verification works on your tenant

Run autonomously checks each step that has an expected result with a separate verification call. On the rehearsal tenant (staging, 2026-11-22) that call failed every time: Behaviour verification said "Verification could not be completed (HttpRequestException)", the step was marked Failed, and the run stopped there – about 40 seconds for a generated test case, at step 1. Steps without an expected result ran and passed. It happened for learner and admin runs alike, so it isn't a rights problem.

What we did for the Trainer Demo backup: Submit Over-65 Request (ATBT:9 on the rehearsal tenant) has expected results only on the last step. Autopilot then ran steps 1–10 (Passed) and marked the decision step Failed, with its comment "The result page displays the decision message: Congrats! You've been approved…" and a screenshot of the approval page – the evidence step 5 needs, even though the verification call itself still reported the error.

The day before the class, run one learner-generated test case autonomously. If its first step with an expected result fails with that error, plan Run autonomously as a trainer demo from your Trainer Demo backup, tell learners to skip item 1 of step 4, and report it to UiPath support with the execution link.

docs.title: Send learners the prerequisites
docs.text:
✅ Send these one week ahead. Replace <host>, <ORG> and <TENANT> with your Test Cloud host, organization and tenant. Ask each learner to reply with a screenshot of Delegate showing the tenant.

Prerequisites to send learners

SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS
- A Windows laptop or a Mac, for Delegate
    - Windows 10 (version 1903 or later) or Windows 11, 64-bit, with at least 8 GB RAM
    - or a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later), macOS 14 Sonoma or later, and at least 8 GB free disk space
    - Intel Macs are not supported, and Delegate for macOS is in Preview
    - Rights to install apps, or ask your IT team to install UiPath Assistant and Delegate for you
- Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge
    - With the UiPath browser extension (installed with UiPath Assistant – your trainer helps if it's missing)
    - Pop-ups allowed for your Test Cloud URL
- UiPath Assistant with Delegate, latest STS (Short Term Support) installer
    - Windows: in the installer, select Assistant, Delegate & Cartographer
    - Windows download link: https://download.uipath.com/connected-installer/latest/sts/UiPathPlatformSTS.msi
    - Mac: install Delegate for macOS (Preview) as described in https://docs.uipath.com/delegate/standalone/latest/user-guide/installation
- Access to these sites, with no proxy or firewall blocking them
    - Your Test Cloud URL, which your trainer sends you
    - https://uibank.uipath.com
    - https://download.uipath.com (installers and the Delegate connection tool)
    - The npm package registry, https://registry.npmjs.org, used once to install the Delegate connection tool
    - On a company laptop, check with your IT team first
- On the day
    - Screen: never turn off
    - Laptop: never sleep while plugged in

ACCESS AND SETUP (about 30 minutes)
1. Sign in at https://<host>/<ORG>/<TENANT>
   - Open Test Manager. The project list may be empty.
   - Allow pop-ups for the site.
2. Install UiPath Assistant with Delegate
   - Windows: in the installer, select only "Assistant, Delegate & Cartographer"
   - Mac: Delegate for macOS (Preview), Apple silicon, macOS 14 or later
3. In Assistant, sign in to <ORG> / <TENANT>. In Delegate, choose the QA / Testing profile.
4. Connect Delegate to Test Manager (one time, about 5 minutes):
   follow the "Connect Delegate to Test Manager" section of the guide's
   Prerequisites page, with these values:
   - host: <host>
   - organization: <ORG>
   - tenant: <TENANT>

VERIFICATION
- Delegate answers "List the tenant I am connected to." with <ORG> / <TENANT>
- The UiPath extension is enabled in the browser profile you'll use
- Reply with a screenshot of that Delegate answer
- If step 4 fails, send a screenshot and bring your laptop 30 minutes early

Check the Delegate connection on real laptops

The connection step was checked against the docs and the official installers, not yet on a learner laptop. Before the first class, spend 15 minutes on one Windows and one Mac laptop: Windows package manager allowed, the admin prompt for Node.js, the company proxy, the browser sign-in, Delegate finding the tool after Assistant restarts, the QA / Testing profile, and the Delegate for macOS (Preview) DMG.

Mac learners

✅ Machine: Apple silicon (M1 or later), macOS 14 Sonoma or later. Intel Macs aren't supported.

✅ Delegate for macOS (Preview): DMG for Enterprise organizations, PKG for Community. Tell Mac learners which installer to use and where to get it: point them to Install and update (Enterprise: UiPath Assistant (arm64).dmg; Community: the UiPath Platform Installer for macOS PKG). Put the exact download link in the prerequisites message. If it doesn't work, the learner uses the browser path and pairs with a neighbour for the Delegate parts.

✅ Everything else runs in the browser or on your cloud robots.

docs.title: Known caveats
docs.text:
✅ The sample project pre-fills old values. The .tmh pre-fills Name UiBank Project, Prefix UIBWS, and a description written for a developer workshop. Step 1 tells learners what to type instead. Re-export a business-version .tmh when you can.

✅ Imported history is 3 years old. The Dashboard (Daily / Weekly only, no custom date range) never shows it, and Execution Insights "From last N days" ignores it. Step 8 uses From selection or From last day.

✅ Imported results show the original tester's name under Executed By. Crop it from any screenshot you share.

✅ Chat Edit mode asks Accept / Reject for every tool call, reads included: about 5 clicks for the overview prompt, 5–7 for the triage prompt and 7 for the step 8 table prompt. The learner pages warn about it.

✅ No chat tool starts, schedules or stops runs, or creates Execution Insights with the standard Test Manager tools. Learners use the buttons for those.

docs.text:

4-hour version

Steps 1, 2 and 3; step 4 with Execute Manually and Delegate only; the linking part of step 6 (learners link 3 test cases – skip the Studio Web demo); steps 7, 8 (charts and Insights) and 9. Run autonomously and Exploration are demos from the Trainer Demo project.

docs.title: Trainer notes
docs.text:
Delegate security questions

Use these if a customer's IT or security team asks about Delegate.

✅ Data: the task text and screenshots go to the AI model through the AI Trust Layer. UiPath is contractually barred from training on customer data.

✅ Storage: conversation history is stored in the tenant's region until the user deletes it. A local-only setting keeps history on the laptop.

✅ Encryption: TLS 1.2 or later in transit, AES-256 at rest.

✅ Access: Delegate runs as the signed-in user, without elevated rights. Entering a password always needs an explicit approval.

✅ Network: outbound HTTPS only, to UiPath domains. Delegate uses the system proxy and the company's root certificates.

✅ Admin control: Automation Ops can enforce and lock Delegate settings, including approval mode and which models are allowed.

✅ Compliance: SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018 and 42001, HIPAA and others. Delegate falls under the existing Automation Cloud DPA (Data Processing Agreement).

See Security overview, Data security and compliance and Configuring the firewall.

Autopilot chat governance and cost talk-track

✅ Chat acts as the signed-in user, with that user's permissions. The AI Trust Layer audit log records its operations.

✅ Edit mode asks before each tool; Agent mode runs tools without asking. The workshop stays in Edit mode.

✅ Cost in one line: chat turns and Delegate tasks use the learner's AI usage pool; the Autopilot buttons don't; robot runs use Platform Units, and autonomous runs use App Test Platform Units.

docs.title: Day-before checklist
docs.text:
✅ UiBank still has the defect: apply for a loan at UiBank with age 66. It must show "Congrats! You've been approved…". If UiBank now rejects it, there is no UiBank defect for the NO-GO: use Submit High-Volume Request as the failing test instead, and tell learners. Keep the reference go/no-go report at hand to show what the NO-GO looked like with the over-65 defect.

If UiBank fixed the over-65 defect

An untested emergency path: this switch was not run on the tenant (UiBank still had the over-65 defect on 2026-11-22). Try it on the Trainer Demo project before you hand it to learners.

  1. Learners edit steps 6, 8 and 11 of their own Submit High-Volume Request to 150000, 500000 and "Verify 'Congrats! You've been approved…'" – the same data as your automation.
  2. In step 6, they link Submit High-Volume Request instead of Submit Over-65 Request.
  3. In step 7, they add it to the set in place of Submit Over-65 Request.
  4. In step 9, they expect NO-GO on the criterion "Applicants 18-65 years old, requesting >$100,000 with income >3x loan amount: Approve".

✅ Loan Lookup: submit one loan and check that its loan ID opens under Already Have A Loan?. Step 9's Delegate repro uses it.

✅ Report location: on a lab laptop, ask Delegate to save a test file on the Desktop and check where it lands. OneDrive can redirect the Desktop.

✅ VM pool: availability profile and Max number of VMs set for the class size (1 VM per 4–5 learners); Platform Units balance checked.

✅ Pre-warm done: 3 Run autonomously runs and 1 Exploration, timed.

✅ Learner-like account pass (an account with only the learner group's rights): Default Folder picker shows the folder, and after Save and a reload the field still shows it (no "Folder does not exist." toast); the chat prompts of steps 1, 7, 8 and 9 give the expected answers; Select Automation lists UiBank.BusinessTests; the serverless run gives 2/1/0; Generate Report → From selection works; one Run autonomously of a learner-generated test case gets past its first expected result (see the warning under Pre-warm); the learner can open your completed over-65 run in the Trainer Demo project; usage pool left.

✅ Screenshots: if labels changed since the guide was written, note them and tell learners at the start.

During the session

✅ Watch Orchestrator → Jobs in the workshop folder before and after lunch.

✅ Start the Exploration demo only when the Run autonomously queue has drained.

✅ Watch the usage pool and the App Test Platform Units balance.

docs.title: After the workshop
docs.text:
✅ Revert the VM pool: availability profile Balanced, Max number of VMs back to 1 (or delete the pool).

✅ Clean up: learner projects, any schedules learners created, Delegate routines, governance settings, Studio Web projects, and the serverless machine and robot account if you won't reuse them. Granted top-ups can't be returned.

✅ Remove learners from the group, or delete the tenant.

Back to Home

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Do this checklist at least a few days before the workshop. It takes about 30 minutes. Most of the day runs in your browser; the only thing you install is UiPath Assistant with Delegate, plus a one-time connection to Test Manager.

When you're done, send your trainer a screenshot of Delegate showing your tenant (see Ready?).

Labels may differ

This workshop runs on a tenant with the latest features. Your screens may show slightly different labels. Features marked (Preview) may still change.

    • Windows: in the installer, select Assistant, Delegate & Cartographer
    • Windows download link: https://download.uipath.com/connected-installer/latest/sts/UiPathPlatformSTS.msi

On the day, Delegate works on your screen while you watch, so your laptop must stay awake and unlocked. Turn screen lock back on after the workshop.

How to keep the screen on (Windows 11)
  1. Open Start → Settings → System → Power & battery → Screen, sleep, & hibernate timeouts.
  2. Under Plugged in, set Turn my screen off after and Make my device sleep after to Never.

On a company laptop, a policy may still lock the screen. Check with your IT team.

How to keep the screen on (macOS)

Open System Settings → Lock Screen and set Turn display off on power adapter when inactive to Never.

On a company Mac, a policy may still lock the screen. Check with your IT team.

docs.title: Accounts and access
docs.text:
Your trainer invites you to the workshop organization and tenant, and sends you the sign-in link. It looks like https://<host>/<ORG>/<TENANT>. For most organizations, the host is cloud.uipath.com.

  1. Open the link and sign in with the account your trainer invited.
  2. Open Test Manager from the left menu. You see the list of Test Manager projects. It may be empty: you create your own project in step 1 of the workshop.
  3. Allow pop-ups for this site, because Test Manager opens the manual test window as a pop-up. In Chrome or Edge: select the icon to the left of the address bar → Site settings (Chrome) or Permissions for this site (Edge) → Pop-ups and redirects → Allow.

Check your licence

The Autopilot icon (a sparkle, top right) appears only inside a project, not on the project list. If a project is already listed, open it and look for the icon. If no project is listed yet, you'll check it in step 1.

No Autopilot icon inside a project? Ask your trainer to check your user licence: you need App Test Developer or App Tester.

Your trainer has prepared the shared workshop folder and the robots in Orchestrator, the part of UiPath where robots and their folders live. You don't set up anything there.

docs.title: Install UiPath Assistant and Delegate
docs.text:
UiPath Delegate is a desktop AI agent. You give it a task in plain words, and it does the work on your machine, in your browser and apps, while you watch. It comes with UiPath Assistant.

flowchart LR
    A["You describe a task<br/>(in plain words)"] --> B["Delegate does it<br/>(browser, apps, Test Manager)"]

For testing, Delegate works with Test Manager: in the workshop it runs a test case on the UiBank website and records the result, and later it reproduces a defect and writes a report.

WindowsmacOS
  1. Download the installer: UiPathPlatformSTS.msi.
  2. Run it, and select only Assistant, Delegate & Cartographer. Robot and Extensions are selected for you. Accept the licence and select Install.
  3. Open UiPath Assistant once it's installed.

Used Delegate during Preview?

Uninstall the Preview build first, then install the current installer. In Delegate, open Settings → General → About and check that the version starts with v26. See Moving from the Preview installer to the GA installer.

Delegate for macOS (Preview)

Delegate for macOS is in Public Preview. It works for the workshop, but screens may change. If it doesn't work on your Mac, every step has a browser path, and you can pair with a neighbour for the Delegate parts.

You need a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later), macOS 14 Sonoma or later, and 8 GB of free disk space. Intel Macs aren't supported.

  1. Install Delegate for macOS as your trainer tells you:
    • Enterprise organizations: the DMG (UiPath Assistant (arm64).dmg). Open it and drag the app to Applications. It doesn't update itself.
    • Community organizations: the UiPath Platform Installer for macOS (PKG).
  2. Open UiPath Assistant from Applications.

See Install and update.

docs.title: Set up Delegate
docs.text:
1. In UiPath Assistant, click the person icon or your initials (top right) → Preferences → Orchestrator connection. Sign in with your workshop account and select the workshop tenant.

    If your trainer gave you a host other than cloud.uipath.com, enter it as the service URL before you sign in. Your trainer tells you what to type.

    Assistant already shows you signed in, but to another tenant?
    1. Click Sign out. Your default browser opens and asks if you want to log out. Don't click it.
    2. In that browser, sign in to the workshop tenant.
    3. Go back to Assistant, click Sign in, and select the workshop tenant.

  2. Select Delegate in Assistant's top ribbon. It appears only once Assistant is connected.

  3. Set the work profile: click your user name (bottom left) → Settings → Behavior preferences, and select QA / Testing.

    Optional: in the same Behavior preferences, pick a plain-language Tone and a shorter Depth.

  4. Click + New in the left panel to start a session. Use this one session for the whole workshop.

  5. Check the model selector next to the chatbox: keep the default or recommended model it offers, unless your trainer names another one. Other models work too, but their answers may differ from the guide's samples.

  6. Choose how much Delegate does on its own: select Adaptive in the mode selector next to the chatbox (or Settings → Security). If you also see a smart option (Smart mode or Smart approvals), leave it on – it also approves what Delegate judges safe.

    Approval mode What Delegate does Cautious Asks before every action. A good choice for regulated teams Adaptive (recommended) Does safe, read-only actions on its own, and asks before anything that writes, changes or runs something Full access Never asks – trusted environments only

Delegate acts on your behalf

It uses your UiPath account and permissions, and every action is logged in your name.

✅ Keep screen context on Default (the screen icon next to the chatbox), so Delegate sees only the apps you attach to the chat.

✅ In Settings → Security → Blocked websites, quick-add Banking, Payments and Password Manager.

✅ Check that the UiPath browser extension is turned on in the browser you'll use: open chrome://extensions (Chrome) or edge://extensions (Edge). If you have several Chrome profiles, use one profile for the whole workshop. Not listed? The extension comes with the UiPath Assistant installer – ask your trainer to help you add it.

docs.title: Connect Delegate to Test Manager (one time, ~5 min)
docs.text:
Delegate talks to Test Manager through a small UiPath command-line tool (CLI – Command Line Interface). You install it once and sign it in once. You copy two lines; you don't need to learn any commands.

Your trainer sends you the host, organization and tenant to use. Keep that message open.

1. Install the tool. Copy the line for your computer, paste it, and press Enter.

WindowsmacOS

Open PowerShell (press the Windows key, type PowerShell, and press Enter). A normal window is fine. Paste:

$env:UIP_SKIP_SKILLS="1"; $env:UIP_SKIP_RUNTIMES="1"; irm https://download.uipath.com/uipath-cli/install.ps1 | iex

If Node.js isn't on your laptop, the script installs it first. Windows may ask Do you want to allow this app to make changes to your device? Select Yes.

Open Terminal (press Cmd + Space, type Terminal, and press Enter). Paste:

curl -fsSL https://download.uipath.com/uipath-cli/install.sh | bash -s -- --skip-skills --skip-runtimes

If Node.js isn't on your Mac, the script installs it first, without asking for your Mac password.

Wait until the script finishes and you see the prompt again. It takes a few minutes. The extra settings in the line skip parts that only developers need.

2. Sign in. Close the window and open a new PowerShell or Terminal window, so it finds the new tool. Paste this line, with the three values from your trainer in place of <host>, <ORG> and <TENANT>:

uip login --authority https://<host> --organization <ORG> --tenant <TENANT>

Your browser opens a UiPath sign-in page. Sign in with your workshop account. When the page says you're signed in, close the tab and go back to the window.

3. Check it worked. In the same window, paste:

uip login status

It shows that you're logged in, with the workshop organization and tenant. Then close the window, and quit and reopen UiPath Assistant, so Delegate finds the tool.

If it fails

Don't spend more than 10 minutes on it. Send your trainer a screenshot of the error, and bring your laptop 30 minutes early on the day: the trainer helps you there. Common causes are a company laptop that blocks installs, or a proxy that blocks downloads. Ask your IT team if you can.

You can still do the whole workshop: every step has a browser path, and for the Delegate parts you can pair with a neighbour.

Signed out later?

The sign-in expires after a while without use. If Delegate later says it isn't signed in, or shows 401 Unauthorized, run the sign-in line from step 2 again (30 seconds).

See Installing Delegate for the testing profile and Testing setup FAQ.

docs.title: Check Delegate
docs.text:
1. In your Delegate session, ask:

    List the tenant I am connected to.

    Delegate replies with your organization, tenant and user name. Wrong tenant? Switch it as in the Assistant already shows you signed in tip, and ask again.

  2. Then ask:

    Check that you can reach Test Manager in my tenant, and list the Test Manager projects I can see.

    Delegate lists the projects, or says the list is empty. Both are fine: it reached Test Manager. If it says it isn't signed in, repeat Connect Delegate to Test Manager.

Delegate asks to approve a command?

Delegate reaches Test Manager by running commands, in PowerShell on Windows or in the shell on a Mac. In Adaptive mode it asks first. You can approve each one, or select Allow Run PowerShell for this session. That lets Delegate run any PowerShell command without asking until the session ends, so choose it only on your workshop laptop.

No Delegate on the day?

Locked-down laptop, Mac problems, or the connection failed? You can still do every step. Steps that use Delegate also have a browser path, and you can pair with a neighbour to watch Delegate work.

docs.title: Test Cloud, Autopilot and Delegate
docs.text:
Use the import time

The project import in step 1 takes a few minutes. Start it first: download and import the project, then come back and read this page while it runs.

docs.title: What is Test Cloud?
docs.text:
Test Cloud is UiPath's cloud platform for application testing. It brings together:

✅ Test Manager – plan, run and analyze your testing, from requirements to results

✅ Studio Web – build automated tests in the browser

✅ Robots – run your tests for you, in the cloud or on a machine your team provides

✅ Agentic Testing – AI agents at every step: Autopilot in Test Manager, and Delegate on your desktop

docs.title: What is Test Manager?
docs.text: Test Manager links requirements to test cases, test sets and results, so you always know what's tested and what's failing. Today you work in your own Test Manager project, with UiBank's loan application as the system under test.

docs.title: Autopilot in Test Manager
docs.text:
Autopilot is the AI built into Test Manager. Its testing capabilities are called Autopilot for Testers. You meet it in two ways.

Autopilot buttons run one fixed task from a button in Test Manager:

✅ Evaluate quality (the + Evaluate quality button on a requirement) – finds gaps in a requirement, such as undefined limits and missing edge cases, and suggests fixes (step 2). See Quality-check requirements.

✅ Generate tests – writes test cases from a requirement and its documents (step 3). See Generate tests for requirement.

✅ Import Test Cases – turns an Excel sheet of test scripts into test cases (optional in step 3). See Import manual test cases.

✅ Execution Insights (the Generate Report button on the Execution page) – a report with the top failing tests, common errors and recommendations (step 8). See Generate test reports.

Autopilot chat is a conversation panel inside your project. Open a project, then select the Autopilot icon in the top bar. You ask in plain language, and chat answers from your real project data. It can search your project, build charts, and make changes for you, such as adding labels or creating a test set. It has two modes: Edit, which asks before each action, and Agent, which acts without asking. Today you stay in Edit mode. See About Autopilot chat and Search Test Manager project.

Check what chat tells you

Chat is fast, but it can be wrong. Compare its counts with the Execution page, and its how-to answers with the docs. The panel says it too: "Autopilot can make mistakes."

docs.title: Delegate on your desktop
docs.text:
Delegate is an AI agent on your laptop. It works in your applications, documents and websites the way you would: it reads the screen, clicks and types. With the QA / Testing profile, it also works with Test Manager. Today Delegate:

✅ Runs a manual test case on the UiBank website and publishes the result to Test Manager (step 4)

✅ Reproduces the defect with screenshots and writes a go/no-go report (step 9)

✅ Optional: turns a business document into a requirement and a test case (step 3)

You choose how often Delegate asks before it acts, and you can stop it at any time. You install it and connect it to Test Manager once, in the Prerequisites. Delegate runs on Windows, and on Macs with Apple silicon as Delegate for macOS (Preview). See the Delegate user guide.

docs.title: Robots
docs.text:
Robots run tests with no one at the keyboard. Your trainer provides them, so you install nothing:

✅ Run autonomously (Preview) – a robot reads your written test steps and follows them on the UiBank website, like a careful new colleague (step 4). Your trainer also demos Autonomous Exploration (Preview), where a robot explores UiBank on its own and reports what it finds (step 5).

✅ Cloud robots – they run the automated tests that automation colleagues build in Studio Web (steps 6 and 7).

docs.title: Which helper when
docs.text: Helper What it's for Where you use it today Autopilot buttons Evaluate a requirement, generate or import test cases, Execution Insights reports Steps 2, 3 and 8 Autopilot chat Questions about your project, search, charts, bulk changes such as labels and test sets Steps 1, 7, 8 and 9 Delegate Work on your desktop, across apps: test runs, evidence, documents Steps 4 and 9 Run autonomously (Preview) A robot runs your written test steps, unattended Steps 4 and 5 Studio Web + cloud robots How automation colleagues make tests repeatable, and run them at scale Steps 6 and 7

docs.title: Buttons vs chat: what uses your AI allowance
docs.text:
Licensing and cost

Each user has a monthly AI allowance, called the AI and Agentic usage pool.

✅ Autopilot buttons don't use it. Evaluate quality, Generate tests, Import Test Cases and Execution Insights don't take anything from your pool when you start them from their own buttons.

✅ Every Autopilot chat turn uses it, even when chat runs the same capability for you. Charts exist only in chat.

✅ Delegate tasks use the same pool.

✅ Robot runs don't use your pool. Run autonomously and Autonomous Exploration use the tenant's App Test Platform Units, and cloud robot runs use Platform Units. That's your trainer's budget.

When your pool runs out, Autopilot chat and Delegate pause until your administrator grants a top-up or the month resets. So when a button does the job, use the button.

See Autopilot usage pool for testing.

docs.title: What is MCP?
docs.text:
When Autopilot chat changes something in your project, it uses a set of approved actions called tools, served by Test Manager's own MCP server (MCP stands for Model Context Protocol, the standard way to connect an AI assistant to a system like Test Manager). The tools come with Test Manager, so there's nothing to set up, and in Edit mode chat names each tool and waits for you to select Accept or Reject. You approve your first changes in step 7.

Test Cloud only

Autopilot chat, its MCP tools, charts, Run autonomously and Autonomous Exploration are available only when Test Manager comes with Test Cloud, on the Unified Pricing licensing plan. They're not available in Test Manager on Automation Cloud, or on the Flex plan. See the Test Manager feature availability page.

Preview

Run autonomously, Autonomous Exploration and Delegate for macOS are Preview features. They work for the workshop, but labels and behavior may change, and your tenant may show slightly different screens.

Rule for today

You decide, the agents assist. Treat everything Autopilot and Delegate produce as a draft. Review generated test cases before you create them, read what chat is about to change before you accept it, and check the numbers before you put them in a report.

That's enough theory – let's get started.

Next → 1. Import Your Project and Meet Autopilot Chat

docs.title: 1. Import Your Project and Meet Autopilot Chat
docs.text:
Leads: All · Tools: Test Manager Autopilot chat

Download the project file Import it into Test Manager Link the workshop folder Open Autopilot chat Ask your first three questions

Why it matters for you: you get your own copy of the UiBank release project, and a chat assistant that answers questions about it in seconds instead of clicking through every page.

You start from a ready-made UiBank project: one requirement, six test cases, a test set, past results and attachments. Start the import as soon as you arrive – it runs in the background while the trainer introduces the day.

docs.title: Download the project file
docs.text:
1. Download Agentic Testing Workshop - Sample Test Manager Project.zip.
  2. Unzip it. You'll import the .tmh file inside.

docs.title: Import it into Test Manager
docs.text:
1. Open Test Manager in the workshop tenant, <ORG>/<TENANT>. Your trainer gives you the link.
  2. On Projects, select Import project, then Add file and select the .tmh file. Keep Target: New project.

  3. The file fills in a name, a prefix and a description. Replace all three, so your project is unique on the shared tenant:

    Field Pre-filled Type instead Name UiBank Project UiBank plus your initials, for example UiBank AS Prefix (the project key) UIBWS UIB plus your initials, for example UIBAS Description a sentence about the original technical workshop Loan application tests for the UiBank 2.4 release decision.

    Use initials, not your full name: everyone on the tenant sees the project list.

  4. Clear Include automation information for test cases (it's checked by default). Leave Import governance information and Import project configuration cleared.

  5. Select Import, then OK when the upload completes.

Important

✅ Clear Include automation information for test cases before you select Import.

✅ The import runs in the background and takes 3–15 minutes (about 3 minutes in rehearsal), longer when the whole class imports at once. Refresh Projects until your project card shows Created on instead of Import in progress…. Don't link the folder or open Autopilot chat before then.

✅ Don't see your card? Search for your project name on Projects. The project Dashboard may show No results: the imported results are older than its date range. You'll see your own results there from step 4 on.

Who ran the old tests?

The imported results keep the name of the person who ran them originally, under Executed By. That's history from the sample project, not a person on your team.

docs.title: Link the project to the workshop folder
docs.text:
To run tests on robots later today, Test Manager needs to know which Orchestrator folder to use. Orchestrator is where the robots live; your trainer set up one shared folder for the class.

It's your turn now!

  1. In your project, go to Project Settings and open the Automation tab.
  2. Set Default Folder to the folder your trainer gives you: in this workshop, ATB - Agentic Testing Workshop. Type part of its name to filter the list.
  3. Click Save. A message confirms Folder updated successfully.

Skipped this step?

Robot runs fail with HTTP 400: Please assign folder to project level before executing testcases.

The workshop folder isn't in the Default Folder list? You're not assigned to it yet. Ask your trainer.

docs.title: Open Autopilot chat
docs.text:
Autopilot chat is an assistant inside Test Manager. You ask in plain words; it reads your project, searches the documentation, builds charts and – with your approval – makes changes.

  1. Open your project first. The Autopilot icon (a sparkle) is in the top bar, next to the notifications bell, and it only appears inside a project – not on the project list.
  2. Select it. The Autopilot panel opens on the right, with the question "How can I assist you with test management?".

  3. Under the text box, check the mode selector. Test Manager offers two modes:

    Mode What it does Today Edit Shows each action Autopilot wants to take and waits for your Accept or Reject ✅ Use this one all day Agent Runs actions without asking Don't use it in the workshop

    If it shows Agent, switch it to Edit.

Edit mode asks for every action – reads included

In Edit mode, Autopilot shows a card for each action it takes in Test Manager – the action's name, "via MCP server: testmanager", and Reject / Accept – even when it only reads your project. One question can ask for 5 or more approvals. Read each card, then select Accept. It's slower, but you always see what Autopilot does on your behalf. Searches and charts run without a card.

These actions are called tools. You'll learn what they are, and what they can't do, in 7. Build and Run the Regression Set.

Every chat turn uses your AI allowance

Each message you send to Autopilot chat uses your AI and agentic usage pool. The dedicated Autopilot buttons you use in steps 2 and 3 don't. Ask focused questions, and don't paste the same prompt twice. See Autopilot usage pool for testing.

Autopilot chat needs Test Manager on Test Cloud. No Autopilot icon? See Troubleshooting and ask your trainer to check your user licence.

docs.title: Ask your first three questions
docs.text: Wait until your project card shows Created on. Then type each prompt into the Autopilot panel and press Enter. Wait for the answer before you send the next one.

docs.title: 1 – A how-to question: check the answer
docs.text:
How do I run a manual test case in Test Manager?

Autopilot answers from what it knows, without a tool card. Don't take the answer at face value. In rehearsal it said you can't run a test case on its own and must add it to a test set first. On Test Cloud that's out of date: you can open the test case's ⋮ menu and select Execute Manually. You'll do exactly that in 4. Run the Test Three Ways.

Think about it

The footer of the panel says "Autopilot can make mistakes. Please double check the responses." Treat chat like a helpful new colleague: fast and usually right, but you check anything you'll act on.

docs.title: 2 – An overview of your project
docs.text:
Give me an overview of this project: the requirements and how many test cases each has, the test sets, and the latest executions.

Autopilot asks you to approve about 5 read actions, one at a time – for example Get_requirements, Get_test_sets, Get_test_executions, Get_assigned_test_case_ids_for_requirement and Get_test_cases. Select Accept on each. The answer takes about 1–2 minutes. It may list only the newest executions, but it states the total: 17.

docs.title: 3 – A coverage gap search
docs.text:
Find all test cases not linked to any requirement.

This starts with Autopilot Search, which runs without a card. Chat may then ask you to approve one read, Get_test_cases, to double-check the result. Select Accept. A test case without a requirement is a gap: nobody can say which business rule it proves.

Check it

Compare Autopilot's answers with the left navigation of your project:

✅ Requirements: 1 – Submit Loan Request, with 6 test cases

✅ Test Cases: 6

✅ Test Sets: 1 – UiBank Smoke Test Set

✅ Execution: 17 executions (the imported history)

✅ The search for unlinked test cases returns none: all 6 are linked to Submit Loan Request. Open Test Cases to confirm.

Counts that don't match? Trust the Test Manager pages, not the chat. Chat can miscount – that's why you check.

docs.title: Nice work!
docs.text:
Your project is imported, linked to the workshop folder, and you've had your first conversation with Autopilot – including one answer you had to correct.

Next → 2. Evaluate the Requirement

docs.title: 2. Evaluate the Requirement
docs.text:
Leads: BA · Tools: Test Manager Autopilot

Evaluate the requirement with Autopilot Turn suggestions into rules Fix the under-18 rule

Why it matters for you: test cases are only as good as the requirement they come from. A vague rule gives vague tests – and arguments at sign-off about what "rejected" was supposed to mean.

Vague or incomplete requirements lead to gaps in testing. Evaluate quality, an Autopilot button in Test Manager, reads a requirement and finds gaps – undefined thresholds, ambiguous input formats, missing edge cases or validation rules – and suggests fixes. You decide which suggestions to keep. Buttons like this one don't use your AI usage pool.

docs.title: Evaluate the requirement with Autopilot
docs.text:
1. Open Requirements → Submit Loan Request.
  2. On the requirement page, select + Evaluate quality, next to the Description heading. (The buttons at the top of the page – + Autonomous Exploration, + Optimize coverage and Assign test case – come later.)

  3. In Provide additional context → Add documents, select these project documents (marked P), so Autopilot checks the requirement against their rules:

    ✅ UiBank Security Guidelines.pdf – input validation rules for the form fields

    ✅ UiBank Accessibility Guidelines.docx – form labels, error messages and keyboard access

    You may also see Project_import_summary_.pdf, created by your import in step 1. Leave it unselected. Where do these documents come from?

    They're the project's attachments, under Dashboard → Attachments. Anyone on the project can add documents there, and Autopilot can read them.

  4. On the next screen:

    1. Select a prompt: choose Multifaceted Audit.

      Editing prompts and adding your own

      The built-in prompts are editable, and you can add custom prompts of your own – for example your team's checklist for requirements. Manage them in the Prompt Library, under Project Settings.

    2. Keep the default model.

    3. Select Evaluate quality. The panel says Evaluating quality and that you can close it. Autopilot takes about a minute, and you're notified when it's done.

  5. Under Latest activity, on the right of the requirement, select Quality enhancements. The Enhancement suggestions panel opens with the list, each with the status To do. If you kept the panel open, it shows them as soon as Autopilot finishes.

    6. See Requirement evaluation.

docs.title: Turn suggestions into rules
docs.text:
A suggestion tells you what's missing. Your job as the analyst is to replace it with the actual business rule.

  1. Expand each suggestion. Select Add to Requirement for the ones you agree with. Its status changes from To do to In work, and its title and suggestion appear at the end of the description.

    Add to Requirement closes the panel: reopen Quality enhancements for the next one.

    Read this before you click Add to Requirement

    With workshop rights, suggestions made by the + Evaluate quality button can't be applied: Add to Requirement and the status drop-down open a page that says "You do not have the necessary rights to access this application." with a Click here to logout button. Suggestions made through Autopilot chat work normally.

    ✅ Don't click Click here to logout. Press the browser Back button, or open the requirement again.

    ✅ Then run the same evaluation in Autopilot chat – see Evaluate in Autopilot chat below – and select its Review link. In that list, Add to Requirement and the status drop-down work: carry on from here.

    ✅ No time for chat? Copy the suggestion's title into the requirement description yourself, write the rule under it (item 3), and skip item 4.

  2. Pick 1–2 suggestions about outcomes or messages, such as boundaries, rejection rules or the result page: you'll replace them with UiBank's exact text.

  3. Edit the requirement. Under each added title, replace the suggestion with the rule itself, using the exact text UiBank shows. Your changes save when you click outside the description.

    Sample: turn a suggestion into a rule

    Your suggestions may differ. This one says rejection rules are missing:

    Applying with its second example in UiBank ($150,000 for 3 years, $400,000 income) gives the exact text. The acceptance criteria already have a rule for this case, with a different message, so update that rule instead of adding one:

    Applicants 18-65 years old, requesting >$100,000 without income >3x loan amount:
Reject with "You must be at least 18 years old for a loan and the loan must not exceed 100k."

  4. Set the status of each suggestion you used to Done, from its status drop-down. Rights page again? You're in the button-made list: use the chat-made list from Review.

Check it

✅ Each title you added has a rule under it, not the suggestion.

✅ Each rule names a boundary you could test (an age, an amount) and the exact message UiBank shows.

docs.title: Evaluate in Autopilot chat
docs.text:
The same request in Autopilot chat – use it if Add to Requirement shows the rights page

Open the Autopilot panel (top bar, Edit mode) and type:

Evaluate the quality of the Submit Loan Request requirement and list the top 5 suggestions.

Autopilot asks you to approve Get_requirements, then shows the card Evaluate Requirement Quality with the requirement, documents, prompt and model it will use. Select Accept each time. After about a minute it says "Evaluated with 14 suggestions" (your number may differ), lists the top 5 and gives a Review button. Review opens the chat-made Enhancement suggestions list, where Add to Requirement works – you see "Suggestion added to the requirement." Chat doesn't change the requirement by itself.

Same result, two ways in: the + Evaluate quality button doesn't use your AI usage pool and lets you pick documents and a prompt; the chat version uses your AI usage pool but fits into a conversation – for example "…and tell me which suggestion matters most for the over-65 rule".

docs.title: Fix the under-18 rule
docs.text:
The original acceptance criteria need the same check. Test cases are generated from the requirement's text, so its messages must match what UiBank shows. The requirement says what UiBank should do: match its wording, not its behavior.

  1. In UiBank, go to Products → Loans → Apply For A Loan. Fill in any email, an amount of 5000, any term, an income of 50000 and an age of 17, then submit. UiBank shows two lines:

    Sorry, at this time you have not been approved for a loan.

    You must be at least 18 years old for a loan and the loan must not exceed 100k.

  2. Edit Submit Loan Request. In the under 18 rule only, replace "Not approved due to age." with UiBank's two lines. For example:

    Applicants under 18 years old: Reject with "Sorry, at this time you have not been approved for a loan." and the reason "You must be at least 18 years old for a loan and the loan must not exceed 100k."

    It saves when you click outside the description.

  3. Leave the over 65 rule exactly as it is. It says what the business wants – a rejection – and you'll test UiBank against it from step 3 on.

Check it

✅ The under 18 rule shows UiBank's two lines, word for word.

✅ The over 65 rule still says "Not approved due to age."

Make every rule measurable

Back at your desk, give every rule the same treatment: exact boundaries (18, 65, $100,000), the exact approval message ("Congrats! You've been approved for a loan with UiBank!") and the exact rejection message. 3. Generate Test Cases generates test cases from this text, so every vague word becomes a vague test step.

docs.title: Nice work!
docs.text:
Your requirement is clearer and testable – ready for generating test cases.

Next → 3. Generate Test Cases

docs.title: 3. Generate Test Cases
docs.text:
Leads: BA · Tools: Test Manager Autopilot Delegate (optional)

Generate test cases with Autopilot Review and keep the best Name your over-65 test case Bring your own sources (optional)

Why it matters for you: writing manual test cases by hand takes days. Here Autopilot drafts them from your requirement in minutes, each one traceable to a business rule – and you stay the one who decides what's good enough.

Generate tests, an Autopilot button in Test Manager, reads a requirement and proposes test cases with manual steps. It works from the requirement you improved in 2. Evaluate the Requirement. You review every proposal before it's saved. The project already has 6 test cases on this requirement; today you add at least 3 more – including the one that decides the release.

docs.title: Generate test cases with Autopilot
docs.text:
1. Open Requirements → Submit Loan Request.
  2. Select + Optimize coverage, then Generate tests. (Assign test case → Generate test cases opens the same panel.)

  3. In Provide additional context → Add documents, select:

    ✅ UiBank Security Guidelines.pdf – input validation rules for the form fields

    ✅ UiBank Accessibility Guidelines.docx – form labels, error messages and keyboard access

    Add documents or Leverage RAG?
